title: Upper Body dominant 4 Days split review
summary: He reviews a subscriber's time-limited, upper-body-focused 4-day split and his earlier rest-pause 25-rep routine. He replaces the rest-pause sets with an AMRAP at 75-85% plus a 60% back-off set, and asks for evolving ranges on squats and antagonist arm supersets. He suggests adding long-head triceps work and much more upper-back volume, since the upper back recovers well from frequent high-volume work.
claims: A 25-rep rest-pause goal with 45-60 second pauses (12+8+5) means you were outside meaningful intensity if you can get 8 more reps; more intense work gives similar hypertrophy with less tonnage and saves time
He trains about three hours but considers himself a special case; most people do not need that long
Regular deadlifts done as strength work should not be done for high reps
The push press is poor for shoulder hypertrophy because you cannot tell how much the legs help; for size, touch-and-go overhead press beats paused because of the stretch and elastic response
25 reps is too high for weighted chin-ups, while 20-rep squats work well with this method
Barbell calf raises for 2x30 are a good high-volume choice for calves
The overhead press needs a mix of intensity and volume to progress; 25 reps is far too high in the volume window
Hamstrings respond very well to high reps; 3x20 good mornings are a good choice
A single set of 20 lateral raises is not ideal: the shoulders are delicate and you may land in an intensity window that risks injury without the stimulus
Band movements should be done with high volume and low intensity
High rep ranges are fine for isolation movements because they are as far from strength work as you can get
Grippers train mainly one part of the forearm; great for grip strength, which helps forearm training, but not the best for hypertrophy
Farmer's walks on rest days are great GPP for grip and conditioning; he cannot do them because the ground is frozen eight months of the year where he lives
Most of bodybuilding is really powerbuilding: you need strength to get bigger and size to get stronger, though he dislikes hybrid labels
Chest and back is a good non-synergistic pairing; synergistic days would be chest with triceps and shoulders, or back with forearms and biceps
Rest-pausing until you hit 25 reps adds weight too slowly and shortchanges progression
Instead do one AMRAP at 75-85% and immediately follow with a set at 60% to failure for extra volume and intensity
Incline dumbbell press for 3x6-10 is an excellent accessory to the barbell bench
Wide-grip barbell upright rows are a good shoulder superset with rows as long as the form is correct
There is no such thing as a quad day; quads, glutes and hamstrings work together, so if you build body part days do it properly
3x10 squats invite even more sandbagging than 3x5; use 4x6-8 or 4x7-10 to keep about 30 reps while allowing progression
Fixed rep ranges are fine for variations like hip thrusts at 3x12, but strength work benefits from evolving ranges
Shoulders and arms is a good split because pressing already uses the triceps
Close-grip bench adds pressing volume without taxing the shoulders and adds triceps work
12-15 reps is as high as you should go with challenging weight when progression is the goal; pump work can go to 50
Barbell cheat curls turn into a supinated clean; dumbbell cheat curls stay closer to a real curl; a cheat curl is a strength movement and a fixed 3x8 offers some injury protection
Do not superset heavy, cheated lateral raises with the overhead press
Superset French press with hammer curls and cheat curls with rope pushdowns; antagonist arm supersets localise the pump and can help growth
Add skull crushers for the long head because French press alone is not enough
The upper back takes a huge amount of volume, recovers fast, and responds to frequency; you can train it almost every day and should add it to light leg days
exercises: leg drive hides shoulder work; poor for hypertrophy
better than paused for size: stretch and elastic response
pressing volume without taxing shoulders, more triceps
barbell version becomes a supinated clean
